Jensen Huang's return as chief executive of Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) sent shares of its Asian partners and suppliers sharply higher on Tuesday.

Asian Markets Rally as US Futures Hold Gains

S&P 500 futures edged up 14.25 points, or 0.20%, to 7,268.75 as of around 7:42 p.m. EST on Monday. The Nasdaq 100 futures climbed 1,751.75 points, or 6.97%, to 26,878.25, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average futures rose 1,447.98 points, or 3%, to 49,595.31.

In Asia, South Korea's KOSPI jumped 5.81%, to 4,982.20, while Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed 3.56%, to 58,446.83 in early Tuesday trade.

Memory Makers and AI Partners Lead Gains

Nvidia's key memory suppliers led the gains, with SK Hynix Inc.'s (NASDAQ:SKHY) Seoul-listed shares jumping 8.02% to KRW 1.17 million ($870.86), and Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. rising 6.82% to KRW 189,600 ($140.95).

In Tokyo, SoftBank Group Corp. gained 4% to JPY 3,146 ($19.78), while Fujitsu Ltd. climbed 1.71% to JPY 3,389 ($21.32).

NVDA Board Reverses Course on Jensen Huang

Just 12 days after accepting Huang's resignation, Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as CEO.

The board said senior U.S. government officials gave input and that it is confident his return poses no national security risk.

Price Action: Nvidia closed 31.48% higher on Monday at $165.05 and climbed 1.05% in after-hours trading at $166.79.

title: Is Amazon's Profit Riskier Than It Looks?

Is Amazon's Profit Riskier Than It Looks?
Trefis Team

Today's big story: Reported SEC Probe: Could Nvidia Stock Fall To $92?

Update, Nov 23: Large tech stocks rose in Monday morning trading after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. Amazon rose about 4%, to about $256, and the Nasdaq 100 fund (QQQ) rose about 7%, while Anthropic was about flat. The figures below are at Friday's close.

Amazon.com (AMZN) closed at $246.82 on Friday, Nov 20. That was a fall of 4.1% for the day. Anthropic (ANT), newly listed, fell 8.5% on its second day of trading. Why mention both? This article looks at how much of Amazon's profit came from gains on stocks and stakes it holds, and what a slide like Anthropic's could mean for that profit.

The answer is a large share. Over the four quarters to September 2026, 40.1% of Amazon's pre-tax income was non-operating income. That is profit from outside the business itself, such as gains on stocks and stakes a company owns. Almost all of it was gains on securities, $69.7 billion.

That is new for Amazon. From 2019 to 2022, non-operating items were a small net loss, -6.0% of pre-tax income. From 2023 to September 2025, they were 9.3% of pre-tax income. So Amazon's reported profit now rises and falls with the prices of what it holds. The income statements do not show which holdings produced the gains. So we do not size any single one, Anthropic included.

Which Quarter Brought In Most Of The Gains?

Most of it came in one quarter. In the three months to June 2026, Amazon's non-operating income was $53.4 billion. That was 66.0% of its pre-tax income. It was also the largest of any quarter since the start of 2019.

Net income that quarter was $62.6 billion. Operating income, the profit from selling goods and services, was $27.5 billion. So net income was 2.3 times operating income.

Amazon's net income in the three months to June was 2.3 times its operating income. If Amazon is a big part of your savings, the profit it reports can drop fast when the stocks it holds fall. When the market has fallen, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio has lost about 81 cents for every $1 its benchmark lost, on average. See the HQ record.

Net income also ran 1.4 times operating cash flow that quarter. Operating cash flow is the cash the business brings in from customers after its running costs.

Did The Gains Keep Coming After June?

No. In the three months to September, Amazon had a non-operating loss of $1.2 billion. Gains on securities became a loss of $0.7 billion. Operating income that quarter was $28.1 billion.

Update, Nov 23: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Nov 22, effective immediately. In Monday morning trading, SPY, a fund that tracks the S&P 500, rose about 5%, leaving it about 7% below its Oct 6 close. That is still below the Oct 6 high, so the bonds-first step below still applies, and the figures are at Friday's close.

The S&P 500 closed at 6,910.39 on Friday, Nov 20. That close was 11.6% below its Oct 6 high. A close 10% or more below a record closing high is called a correction. The Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ is down 19.9% from Oct 6. Gold did not help either. The gold fund GLD fell 15.5% over the same weeks.

You still have to sell something for next year's cash. Our answer is to sell the bond fund first, not the dividend fund. We ran a $2,000,000 portfolio through each correction our funds cover. Selling bonds first ended ahead of an even sale in 7 of 7 cases. Selling the dividend fund first ended ahead in none of them.

The test also found something bigger. How much you hold in stocks mattered more than which fund you sold. That was true in 7 of 7 cases.

How did we run the test?

The portfolio starts at $2,000,000 on the first close of each correction. It holds 40% in an S&P 500 fund, VOO. It holds 20% in a dividend fund, SCHD, and 40% in a bond fund, BND. Each year it pays out $80,000, which is 4% of the start. Dividends are reinvested. We measure the value five years later, or at the Nov 20 close when five years have not passed.

Selling the dividend fund first left the portfolio $24,068 behind an even sale on average. Selling bonds first left it $40,355 ahead on average.

Selling SCHD first during a correction left the portfolio $24,068 behind an even sale on average. The Trefis Income Solution fell less than the S&P 500 in each of the 9 big sell-offs since 2018, and it pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's. See how it held up.

We compared four ways to raise the $80,000. An even sale, called pro rata, takes a slice from each fund in line with its size. Bonds first takes the whole amount from BND while the S&P 500 stays below its old high. Dividend fund first does the same with SCHD. S&P 500 fund first does the same with VOO. Wall Street just put a $1 trillion price on Jensen Huang as Nvidia stock soars 31% after his return as CEO
Joshua Hong

NVDA
^NDX
^GSPC
Trade NVIDIA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Nvidia shares surged more than 31% on Monday after its board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, adding nearly $1 trillion to the chipmaker's market cap and reversing much of the losses that followed his abrupt departure less than two weeks ago.

The rally lifted Nvidia's market value to approximately $4 trillion from roughly $3 trillion at Friday's close. The stock's advance also helped ignite a broader recovery in tech shares, with the Nasdaq 100 climbing 6.8% and the S&P 500 gaining nearly 5% by noon.

"There were definitely a lot of people who wanted him back," Interactive Brokers chief strategist Steve Sosnick told Reuters. "The extent that the administration intervened, the extent that shareholders intervened, it will be impossible to know."

Huang resigned on Nov. 12 following revelations about extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang—a businesswoman alleged to have been tied to Chinese intelligence.

Trump's intervention

On Monday, the board acknowledged receiving input from senior U.S. government officials, saying that information gave it confidence that Huang's return did not pose a national security risk.

That's after the board previously said Huang's return was not the goal. Chairman Harvey Jones told investors during the company's Nov. 17 earnings call that the board had unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and was not intending on reinstating him.

He also emphasized that Nvidia had an experienced leadership team and that the board had launched a search for a permanent CEO, retaining executive-search firm Heidrick & Struggles.

Nvidia's sudden reversal in bringing back Huang followed public pressure from top tech leaders like Elon Musk and from President Donald Trump, who had repeatedly advocated for the ousted CEO's return.

On Sunday, Trump posted on Truth Social that he hoped Nvidia's board would rehire its cofounder. And on Monday, Trump said he convinced the board to bring back Huang—including claiming that a U.S. government investigation had exonerated him and found that he had done nothing wrong. 

"President Trump was totally involved, and this is a great decision by the Nvidia board. We have to protect our geniuses," White House communications director Steven Cheung told Fortune.

Nvidia's leadership crisis 

But the market's enthusiasm doesn't halt the investigations from government officials and within the company itself, however. The company's board said its independent investigation would continue despite his reinstatement.

US technology stocks staged a broad rally Monday, with gains across chipmakers, AI infrastructure providers and software companies adding nearly $2 trillion to the Nasdaq 100's market capitalization as investors welcomed Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA, XETRA:NVD).

The chipmaker was up 32%, making it the strongest performer among major US technology stocks, with shares reaching an intraday high of $171.50.

The rally extended well beyond Nvidia, with investors also piling into companies tied to the artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout.

Dell Technologies Inc (NASDAQ:DELL) jumped 22%, while AI cloud providers Nebius and CoreWeave each gained 21%. Memory makersMicron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU) rose 19%, Marvell Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MRVL) added 18%, and Arm Holdings PLC (NASDAQ:ARM) and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (ADR) (NYSE:TSM) each advanced 16%.

Storage companies also enjoyed strong gains, with Western Digital up 15%, Seagate Technology and SanDisk both rising 14%, and Intel gaining 14%.

Oracle Corp (NYSE:ORCL, XETRA:ORC) climbed 12%, as did Tesla Inc (NASDAQ:TSLA), while Palantir Technologies Inc (NYSE:PLTR) added 10%. Qualcomm Inc (NASDAQ:QCOM, XETRA:QCI) rose 10%, Advanced Micro Devices Inc (NASDAQ:AMD, XETRA:AMD) gained 8%, and Broadcom Inc (NASDAQ:AVGO, XETRA:1YD) advanced 3%.

The scale of the move suggests Huang's return has done more than remove a leadership concern at Nvidia. It has also renewed investor confidence in the broader AI investment cycle, which has come under pressure amid questions over infrastructure spending, financing arrangements and the returns on massive capital commitments.

Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, said Huang's return demonstrated his influence over both Nvidia and the wider AI sector.

She described him as the "godfather of AI", arguing that he has a talismanic influence on the industry and that his reinstatement also shifts the dial for corporate finance.

Brooks noted that Nvidia's board had concluded it could not see a future for the company without its co-founder, despite the serious questions surrounding his departure barely two weeks earlier.

For investors, however, the leadership question is only part of the story.

Antonio Di Giacomo, senior market analyst at XS.com, said the scale of Nvidia's gains highlighted how heavily uncertainty surrounding its leadership had weighed on the stock.

Analysts at BMO and Goldman Sachs also welcomed Huang's return, although questions remain about Nvidia's investment strategy and its exposure to other AI companies.
